observations: Single used headlamp assembly photographed against a cluttered, dusty floor/stock pile background.
Watermark text on the photo reads 'HONDA AND ACURA' – this is an overlay added by the seller, not a manufacturer part-number or VIN plate read from the unit itself.
No visible part number, OEM sticker, or model-specific marking on the headlamp housing or lens.
Lamp appears to have an amber turn-signal section and projector-style lens, consistent with several mid-size sedan/SUV designs but not uniquely identifiable to a specific year or model.
Background shows multiple other disassembled parts, suggesting a scrapyard/breaker stock rather than a single item for sale.
No photo of the car it was removed from, no fitment chart, no close-up of any etched part number.

risks.risk: Exact vehicle model/year fitment unknown, which drives price heavily (comparables range from ~8,000 to 150,000 NGN for similar-looking headlamps).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the OEM part number/sticker on the back of the headlamp, or a photo of the lamp mounted on the donor car's front end.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest plausible generic used-headlamp tier until model is confirmed

risks.risk: Lamp could be damaged, cracked, or have non-functional bulbs/wiring not visible in a single static photo.
risks.proof: Photo of the lamp powered on, plus a close-up of the lens for cracks and connector condition.

risks.risk: Listing text claims a broad range of parts (body, engine, suspension) but only a headlamp is shown, raising doubt about what is actually being offered or in stock.
risks.proof: Additional photos of the other claimed parts (engine, suspension, body panels) actually in seller's possession.
risks.if_unproven: treat listing as covering only the item photographed (headlamp)

proof_requests: Clear photo of the OEM part number or sticker on the headlamp housing to confirm exact make/model/year.
Photo of the headlamp powered on to confirm working bulbs/wiring.
Close-up of the lens and housing for cracks, fog, or water damage.
Photo of the actual car/parts donor to confirm the vehicle model.
response.reason: The headlamp's exact vehicle fitment (which determines its price tier, ranging widely across comparables) cannot be read from the single photo, and no part number or donor-car shot is provided.
